Not published.** Jerry Garcia · Council · challenger. Scored 2 Sep 2026 against **The Program — A City That Works v1.10 (31 Jul 2026)** using the 12-topic template and Decision 14. **The letter on this card is a dash.** An internal proposal sits at the bottom of the page and is Joa's to apply or reject. Evidence base is the authorized 2026 campaign site (homepage, about, all ten dated articles including the 17 Aug right-to-cool and Crime Watch pieces, and the 19 Jul launch release) plus the empty VoteMate profile. Challenger: no 2022–26 City term, so no Record lines and no incumbent haircut. 2026 plan taken at face value. ## Card
Field Value
Name Jerry Garcia
Office Council
Kind chal (no 2022–26 City term — 2026 plan taken at face value, no record haircut)
Platform URL (2026) [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/)
Platform lastmod not published on the site (dynamic). Dated posts: launch release 19 Jul 2026 · tax and plans articles 22 Jul 2026 · affordability / businesses / housing-crisis / decline 14 Aug 2026 · right-to-cool, Crime Watch, and press-release page 17 Aug 2026 · bike-lanes 31 Aug 2026.

### The five doors (front of the live card) Each door is **said / record / yes / —**: a sourced sentence or a fact. Never a second grade.
Door Measure said / record / yes / — sentence or fact URL date
Tax cap M66 **said** "Property tax increases / Variable / ≤ Inflation" on the recommended 2035 affordability dashboard. A target, not a cap formula, not a glide path, not a covenant. "I would recommend" is not a commit to lock the residential rate. [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/affordability-in-victoria/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/affordability-in-victoria/) 14 Aug 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
Downtown order M26 / M27 **said** "Visible foot patrols and community safety teams." Not a Public Order Team and not bylaw hours. The 17 Aug Crime Watch article specifies a volunteer observe-and-report Community Safety Patrol under VicPD, still not unified command and still not 6am–10pm bylaw. Door is said, not a grade. [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/) retrieved 2026-09-02
Housing M6 **said** "The objective is to increase supply across every housing type." No unit volume, no 25/20/15 composition, no tenure-share target. [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/affordability-in-victoria/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/affordability-in-victoria/) 14 Aug 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
Household bill M66d **—** Water, sewer, stormwater and the combined household number do not appear. — —
Written program — **yes** An authorized campaign site with five named outcomes, an about page, ten dated articles through 31 Aug 2026, and a 19 Jul launch release. Written and current. Hard targets without published baselines, agencies, funding or a year-path. VoteMate profile is empty (no promises, no biography). Site described on the ACTW profile as "Jerry 1.0" with a second version promised. [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/) retrieved 2026-09-02
## The 12 topics Column key: **answer** = the mark · **quote or fact** = the verbatim sentence, then context · **URL** · **date** = lastmod, retrieved. A dash is unknown, not a fail. ### 1 · Housing that gets built
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
1 M6 housing supply + composition **Partial 1.0** "The objective is to increase supply across every housing type." · Commits × Neither: volume without a unit target and without 25/20/15 (or any) composition shares. Context, same article, not scored separately: market, purpose-built rental, co-ops, non-profit, workforce, missing-middle and secondary suites are listed as types. Homepage "More attainable housing" is the same cell. [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/affordability-in-victoria/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/affordability-in-victoria/) 14 Aug 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
2 M6b land bank + co-ops — Co-ops appear only as a housing type inside the sentence already scored on row 1. No City land bank, acquisition fund or co-op financing instrument. — —
3 M7 permits + AI pre-screening **Partial+ 1.5** "Cut permitting times by at least 50%." · Commits × Target, no instrument: a hard cut with no category clocks and no AI pre-screening. Context, same topic, not a second mark: affordability dashboard "Average permit approval / Months / <90 days"; "Digitize approvals" is adjacency to AI pre-screening, not the named instrument, so it does not lift the cell to Close. FLAG: no baseline year. [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/) retrieved 2026-09-02
4 M7b pattern-book housing — Pre-approved designs do not appear. Homepage, about, five outcomes and all dated articles checked. — —
5 M8/M8b 5% vacancy, DCC cuts, suite amnesty **Partial+ 1.5** Affordability dashboard: "Rental vacancy rate / \~Healthy 3–5% target / 3–5%." · Commits × Target: the 5% vacancy number is named. No DCC cut and no suite amnesty. Secondary suites sit inside the row-1 type list, not as an amnesty instrument. [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/affordability-in-victoria/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/affordability-in-victoria/) 14 Aug 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
### 2 · Downtown order
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
6 M26 Public Order Team — "Visible foot patrols and community safety teams" is not a Public Order Team (unified command / co-location / downtown operations desk). The 17 Aug article proposes a volunteer observe-and-report Community Safety Patrol under VicPD; that is still not POT. Mentions do not resolve up. Door is said, this cell is a dash. — —
7 M26b civilian crisis response — Crime Watch "community support teams could also provide information and referrals to shelters, outreach services, crisis programs, and mental health resources when appropriate" is a referral mention, not civilian crisis dispatch (CRCL / IMCRT / VICOT). Mentions, so a dash. — —
8 M27 bylaw hours 6am–10pm — No bylaw-enforcement hours position. Homepage, about, five outcomes and all dated articles checked. — —
9 M28 data-targeted enforcement — "Focus enforcement on repeat offenders and organized crime" raises targeting without a data instrument. Mentions, so a dash. — —
10 M33 daytime sheltering bylaws — No daytime-sheltering bylaw position. The 14 Aug decline essay names encampments as a symptom of lowered standards; that is frame, not a bylaw instrument. — —
11 M33b drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure) — "Open drug use" in the decline essay is a diagnosis. No protected-list, no bylaw/DPOT, no VicPD/CDSA coordination. Mentions, so a dash. — —
12 M34–M37 encampments, reclaiming spaces, night lighting — Decline essay: encampments "would have been considered unacceptable." Frame and tone, not a named-space reclaim, encampment protocol, or night-lighting programme. Lighting in "Better lighting, cleaning, and rapid graffiti removal" is scored once, on row 26. — —
### 3 · Household bill
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
13 M66 tax glide path (capped on the residential rate) **Partial 1.0** Affordability dashboard: "Property tax increases / Variable / ≤ Inflation." · Agrees × Target = Partial 1.0. "I would recommend" is not Commits to a cap, formula, year-path or override rule. Context, 22 Jul article, not scored separately: "Victoria doesn't need higher taxes to become stronger. It needs a stronger economy." [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/affordability-in-victoria/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/affordability-in-victoria/) 14 Aug 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
14 M66b/c over-collection refund + debt rule — No over-collection refund, no debt rule, no supermajority override. — —
15 M66d the Household Bill — The combined household number, water, sewer and stormwater do not appear. — —
16 M70/M70b provincial downloading ledger **Partial 1.0** "Increase our fair share of funding from senior governments." · Commits × Neither: a funding-share ask with no ledger, no refusal threshold and no published transfer table. Distinct sentence from the downtown-vacancy row. [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/) retrieved 2026-09-02
17 M70c CRD cost and the Goldstream plant — He is also running for the CRD and names regional challenges (homelessness, housing, transportation, infrastructure, emergency planning, economic development). That is a reason to seek the seat, not a CRD-cost position or a Goldstream-plant position. Mentions, so a dash. — —
18 M71–M73d business, downtown, one mandate not a new office **Partial+ 1.5** Affordability dashboard: "Downtown commercial vacancy / Reduce / <6%." · Commits × Target. No Strategic Economic Plan and no one-mandate-not-a-new-office. Context, not scored separately: "Make Victoria the easiest city in B.C. to start and grow a business"; "Revitalize downtown as the region's economic engine"; 14 Aug businesses essay on vacant storefronts and simpler permits (permits already on row 3). [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/affordability-in-victoria/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/affordability-in-victoria/) 14 Aug 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
19 M74/M75/M76 capital threshold, short-stay parking (15-min grace; first-hour gated Year 2), permit fees — "Smarter parking management" and "Better traffic flows and parking options, assisted by smart city technology" raise parking without a 15-minute grace, without first-hour (and first-hour is Year 2 gated anyway), without a capital-approval threshold and without a permit-fee schedule. Mentions, so a dash. No first-hour scored as Year 1. — —
### 4 · Host Nations
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
20 M1–M5 Host Nations Foundation. Topic never drops out of the 12. A dash is still allowed on M1–M5. — No Host Nations, government-to-government, procurement, place-name or urban-Indigenous-liaison position. Topic stays in the 12 as a dash. — —
### 5 · Homelessness and waitlists
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
21 M9/M9b/M64 tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated) **Close 2.0** "Victoria should adopt a right-to-cool policy this year. Every tenant should have the right to protect themselves from dangerous indoor heat by using safe portable cooling equipment." · Commits × Comparable: a tenant-side cooling right named for this year. Not STR, not demoviction, not a 26°C building standard. Context, same article: "But Council should stop short of imposing mandatory indoor temperature standards until it understands what Victoria's older rental buildings can realistically support." Deferral of a building-temperature rule pending a stock assessment is compatible with M64's 26°C gate; it is not Disagrees with heat protection. Face-test for Opposed fails. Prior 404 was the wrong slug (space around "but"); live URL has no space. [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/victoria-needs-a-right-to-cool-policybut-it-must-be-practical/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/victoria-needs-a-right-to-cool-policybut-it-must-be-practical/) 17 Aug 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
22 M10 transparent algorithmic waitlists — No waitlist, allocation-algorithm or published-rules position. — —
23 M11 Housing First + STEP throughput **Close 2.0** "The goal should be permanent housing with the supports people need to remain housed. The target is to reduce homelessness by 85%." · Commits × Comparable: Housing-First-like with a numeric target, not STEP throughput and not −50% unsheltered. No baseline year, agency, treatment capacity or definition of "homelessness reduced." FLAG unverified baseline. Context, same outcome, not scored separately: expand supportive and transitional housing; increase detox, treatment and recovery; coordinate governments around shared outcomes tied to funding. [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/) retrieved 2026-09-02
### 6 · Families
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
24 M12/M13b/M13c childcare, doctors, youth (M13 school food is \$0 → M13d) **Partial 1.0** "Create integrated community health centres." · Commits × Neither: a doctors/clinic goal with no Colwood-style municipal clinic instrument, no childcare and no 18–25 cohort. Context, not a second mark: affordability dashboard "Family doctor attachment / Improve / 95%+" is largely provincial delivery. M13 school food is \$0 and lives on M13d. [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/) retrieved 2026-09-02
25 M13d standing School District 61 agreement — Schools and SD61 do not appear. — —
### 7 · Streets and mobility
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
26 M14/M16/M17/M18 cleanliness and the public realm **Close 2.0** "Better lighting, cleaning, and rapid graffiti removal." · Commits × Comparable: graffiti and cleaning named. Distinct homepage bullet from "Visible foot patrols." Lighting in this sentence is used here, not on M30 or M34–M37 (one sentence, one measure). Context, decline essay, not scored separately: overflowing garbage as a symptom of lowered standards. [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/) retrieved 2026-09-02
27 M19/M22/M38/M40–M42b mobility + Vision Zero (M39 30 km/h struck; calming is M38) **Partial 1.0** "My approach is practical: complete a connected cycling network, require transparent analysis for major corridors and publish before-and-after results." · Commits × Neither: a cycling-network plus analysis programme, not Vision Zero, not adaptive signals, not an M38 inventory. M39 30 km/h is struck — not scored. Transit-priority language in a later paragraph of the same article is scored on row 28, not here. [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/bike-lanes-should-make-victoria-work-betternot-create-new-bottlenecks/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/bike-lanes-should-make-victoria-work-betternot-create-new-bottlenecks/) 31 Aug 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
28 M20b/M23b walking and transit the City controls **Partial 1.0** "High capacity transit also deserves priority." · Commits × Neither: transit priority on constrained corridors is a City street lever, with no sidewalk-gap standard and no list of City-controlled transit instruments. Distinct paragraph from the cycling-network sentence on row 27. Context, same article: Route 95 boardings; hierarchy "safety … followed by transit priority where it moves large numbers of people." Contested: could be argued down to Weak 0.5 as a goal without a tool. [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/bike-lanes-should-make-victoria-work-betternot-create-new-bottlenecks/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/bike-lanes-should-make-victoria-work-betternot-create-new-bottlenecks/) 31 Aug 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
29 M24b/M25b accessibility and public washrooms — Accessibility and public washrooms do not appear as a City programme. Cook Street "accessibility improvements" describes the City's current project, not his ask. — —
30 M25 fix roads first — "Integrate cycling with … scheduled road maintenance" mentions maintenance as a cycling-delivery vehicle, not a backlog, pothole standard or roads-first sequencing rule. Mentions, so a dash. — —
### 8 · Policing and published safety
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
31 M28b business security cost-spreading — Crime Watch "business safety teams" with DVBA is partnership, not cost-spreading of private security. Business-security costs do not appear. — —
32 M28d community paramedicine — Community paramedicine is not named. Referrals in the Crime Watch article are on row 7 as a dash, not here. — —
33 M29/M29b VicPD funding + regional review (convene-and-publish; no binding other force) — "Complementing, not replacing, the important work of Victoria PD" supports current policing as background to a volunteer add-on. No funding-formula settlement and no convene-and-publish regional review. Two years as a VicPD Crime Watch volunteer is professional/community background, which the rules exclude. — —
34 M30 smart LED lights, no surveillance — Lighting sits inside the sentence already scored on row 26. One sentence, one measure. No smart-LED specification and no surveillance limit. — —
35 M31/M31b/M31c/M32 safety dashboard, published enforcement record, crime target **Partial+ 1.5** Affordability dashboard: "Crime severity / Reduce / −30%." · Commits × Target. No published enforcement record. Public performance dashboards are scored on row 42, not here. Crime Watch "publish public performance dashboards" is the same M67 claim. [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/affordability-in-victoria/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/affordability-in-victoria/) 14 Aug 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
### 9 · Beauty as a public good
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
36 M43–M46b heritage and cultural venues — Heritage standards, street furniture and cultural venues do not appear. "One of Canada's most beautiful cities" is tone. — —
37 M45b/c pedestrianisation and the signature project — Pedestrians appear in the bike article as one mode among many, already inside the mobility essay. No pedestrianisation programme and no signature-project shortlist. — —
38 M47–M49 heritage incentives, lighting, parks — "Parks and public spaces" under complete neighbourhoods is a mention, not a parks programme, heritage incentive or ornamental-lighting plan. Lighting already used on row 26. — —
39 M50/M50b/M51/M52 culture, sport, and the arts funding floor — A stronger economy "provides the resources to invest in … arts and culture" is prosperity-funds-arts, not a funding floor. Mentions, so a dash. — —
### 10 · A smaller scored Hall
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
40 M15 managed competition — Competitive testing of City services does not appear. — —
41 M65 rotating zero-based reviews — "Evidence-based budgeting" is frame/tone, not a rotating zero-based cycle, grant test or three-part test. Mentions dash every column. — —
42 M67 quarterly performance dashboard **Close 2.0** "Public performance dashboards." · Commits × Comparable: dashboards named, not the quarterly KPI set. Distinct from the crime-target row. Context, not scored separately: "Residents deserve to know how initiatives are progressing, what outcomes are being achieved and whether public investments are delivering value"; Crime Watch repeats dashboards as a programme feature; success measures include citizen satisfaction and quality-of-life surveys (those sit here as dashboard KPIs, not as M82). [https://jerryforvictoria.ca/](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/) retrieved 2026-09-02
43 M68 overhead reduction by attrition — Headcount, attrition and administrative overhead do not appear. "Control spending growth" is inside the tax/efficiency essay already used on row 13. — —
44 M69 real-estate rationalisation — City real-estate holdings do not appear. Strata-council experience is professional background, which the rules exclude. — —
45 M53/M53b/M53c GIS, AI consultation imagery, LIDAR — "Smart city technologies to improve service delivery" and "assisted by smart city technology" are adjacency to GIS/LIDAR, not named instruments. Adjacency is not a source. — —
46 M53d published municipal AI standard — Municipal use of AI, and a published AI standard, do not appear. "Digitize approvals" is already context on row 3. — —
47 M54–M57 local-tech procurement, open data, Wi-Fi, EV charging — Procurement, open data, public Wi-Fi and EV charging do not appear. Accenture / technology-sector background is professional background, which the rules exclude. — —
### 11 · Climate and trees as operations
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
48 M58/M58b/M64b climate, district energy, seismic — "Expand innovation, technology, ocean and clean-energy sectors" is an economic-development line, already in the economy outcome used on rows 1 and 18, not a Climate Leadership Plan, district-energy or seismic instrument. The 22 Jul plans essay lists climate action among plans others have written. Mentions, so a dash. — —
49 M59–M63 trees, mode share, ecosystems, emergency preparedness — Emergency planning is named as a reason to run for the CRD, not as a City preparedness instrument. Mode share sits inside the bike article already scored on rows 27–28. No 5,000-tree target, no canopy, no ecosystems programme. Community solar as a past business is professional background. — —
### 12 · Neighbourhoods and integrity
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
50 M77/M78/M78b \$25M referendum threshold, 5-step process, material-change rule — "Major projects must all be properly planned and managed so taxpayers receive better value and projects are delivered on time and within budget" is project-management tone, not a \$25M threshold, 5-step sequence or material-change rule. — —
51 M79/M79b Integrity Commissioner + 60-day consultation response — No Integrity Commissioner and no 60-day consultation-response standard. "Remain accountable for results" is tone. — —
52 M79c–f lobbyist registry, FOI fee, remuneration — Lobbyist registry, FOI fee and remuneration do not appear. — —
53 M80/M80b/M80c neighbourhoods, language access, Local Area Plans — "Improve quality of life across all 12 neighbourhoods" and named patrol neighbourhoods in the Crime Watch article are geography, not a neighbourhood-grant line, language-access standard or Local Area Plan programme. Mentions, so a dash. — —
54 M82/M82b community surveys, turnout and ballot access — Quality-of-life surveys and citizen satisfaction are success measures already sitting as dashboard KPIs on row 42. No turnout, advance-vote or ballot-access instrument. One sentence, one measure. — —
55 M81 Saanich amalgamation (one line, not the whole topic) — Amalgamation does not appear. — —
## Working notes (internal, not for the cell) - **Sources read in full:** [campaign home / five outcomes](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/) (retrieved 2026-09-02) · [about](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/about-jerry/) · [articles index](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/) · [affordability, 14 Aug 2026](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/affordability-in-victoria/) · [tax, 22 Jul 2026](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/victoria-cant-tax-its-way-to-prosperity/) · [plans, 22 Jul 2026](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/victoria-has-plans-now-we-need-results/) · [bike lanes, 31 Aug 2026](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/bike-lanes-should-make-victoria-work-betternot-create-new-bottlenecks/) · [right-to-cool, 17 Aug 2026](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/victoria-needs-a-right-to-cool-policybut-it-must-be-practical/) · [Crime Watch, 17 Aug 2026](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/victoria-can-build-a-safer-community-by-learning-from-another-community-crime-watch/) · [strong businesses, 14 Aug 2026](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/strong-businesses-build-strong-communities/) · [housing crisis, 14 Aug 2026](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/victorias-housing-crisis-isnt-just-about-housing/) · [decline, 14 Aug 2026](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/victoria-has-become-comfortable-with-decline/) · [press / launch, 19 Jul 2026](https://jerryforvictoria.ca/articles/press-release/) · [VoteMate 13550](https://votemate.org/bc2026/candidates/13550) (empty: no promises, no biography) · [ACTW live profile](https://acitythatworks.ca/profiles/garcia). - **Not a source, applied:** Accenture / engineering / five businesses / Camosun teaching / Douglas magazine / two years VicPD Crime Watch volunteer / strata-council chair / Institute for Work & Health (professional and community background); Facebook and Instagram linked, not used for a cell; "do not touch social"; Livable CRD questionnaire exists as a form, no Garcia answers published. - **One sentence, one measure — the ledger.** Fourteen sentences carry the fourteen scored cells: (1) increase supply across every housing type → row 1. (2) Cut permitting times by at least 50% → row 3. (3) Rental vacancy 3–5% → row 5. (4) Property tax ≤ inflation → row 13. (5) Fair share of senior-government funding → row 16. (6) Downtown commercial vacancy <6% → row 18. (7) Right-to-cool this year via portable equipment → row 21. (8) Permanent housing with supports / 85% homelessness reduction → row 23. (9) Integrated community health centres → row 24. (10) Better lighting, cleaning, and rapid graffiti removal → row 26. (11) Connected cycling network + corridor analysis → row 27. (12) High capacity transit deserves priority → row 28. (13) Crime severity −30% → row 35. (14) Public performance dashboards → row 42. - **Adds vs the prior 12/55 pass on this page:** row 21 Close (right-to-cool; previous 404 was the wrong slug) and row 28 Partial (transit priority, distinct paragraph). Mean holds C. - **Contested allocations.** Row 21 Close 2.0 is the new high-leverage cell: portable-AC right is comparable to indoor-heat protection, and gating a building-temperature standard behind a stock assessment matches "26°C gated." An Opposed reading ("stop short of mandatory indoor temperature") fails the face-test. Row 28 Partial 1.0 is the most likely to be argued down to Weak 0.5 (goal, no City-lever list) or into row 27; dropping it leaves n=13, mean 1.46, still C. Row 3 stays Partial+ 1.5: "Digitize approvals" is adjacency to AI pre-screening, not Close. - **Dropped / not resolved-up.** M26/M27 from patrols and from Crime Watch volunteers (field-propose; Mentions ≠ resolve-up). M65 from "evidence-based budgeting" (tone). M53 from "smart city" (adjacency). M75 from "smarter parking" (no 15-min grace; first-hour is Year 2 gated and is not present). M80 from "12 neighbourhoods" (geography, not LAPs/grants). M34–M37 from the decline essay (frame). - **Actions found that contradict a 2026 sentence:** none. No City office held 2022–26. No Record haircut. - **Never-list:** no Lisnard / Estrosi / Knafo / Musk / Brivael / Poilievre language used as a source or analogy. - **Rows to put to the candidate before publication:** baselines, year, agency and funding for 85% homelessness and 50% permit cut · is ≤inflation a multi-year covenant or a dashboard wish · POT vs volunteer Community Safety Patrol · v2 date · 26°C building standard after the stock assessment, yes or still no. - **Next mandatory re-check:** after nominations close **11 Sep 2026**, and immediately on any Jerry 2.0. - M83 (civic access / public correction, \$0) has no cell in this 55. Not scored. ## INTERNAL proposed letter — not the live letter **PROPOSE: C** · n = 14 · mean 1.43 Close 2.0 ×4 (rows 21, 23, 26, 42) · Partial+ 1.5 ×4 (rows 3, 5, 18, 35) · Partial 1.0 ×6 (rows 1, 13, 16, 24, 27, 28). Sum: 8.0 + 6.0 + 6.0 = **20.0** across **14** scored cells. Mean **1.429**, band **C** (1.25–1.49). C is already a live letter, so no mapping step. **This is a proposal, not the live letter.** The card above shows **—**. The live letter waits for Joa's click and compute must not overwrite it. Alignment compute APPLIED for Garcia stays **C**. **What the proposal is measuring.** Hard targets without instruments, plus one Close on tenant cooling and one Close on Housing-First-like homelessness. Forty-one dashes. A v2 with baselines, category clocks, POT, tax formula or STEP would move the letter; more targets would not. **Fragility.** Drop row 28 and the mean is 1.46, still C. Drop row 21 to Partial+ and the mean is 1.39, still C. Upgrade row 3 to Close and the mean is 1.46, still C. The letter is not fragile inside this pack.
